boundaries: No claim of kernel NOREPLACE or isolation from same-UID code that ignores the cooperative lock.
The 33/34 host results exercise unchanged product control flow with explicit Android API mocks, not ART/OEM descriptor semantics or SAF behavior.
Hbv/Passkey/Session/DocumentIO compile dependencies are mocks; no password decryption, credential, CM or device qualification follows.
The actual r6 observation remains PUBLISH_LINK/ERRNO/EACCES; upstream sepolicy consistency is an inference, not an observed OEM AVC.
The separate Linux fcntl close experiment supports the admission design but is not an Android runtime result.
No external independent security review is claimed.

review_checks: The process-wide nonblocking admission token precedes all lockfile opens and remains owned through uncertain lock cleanup.
A second local Guard is rejected before any new descriptor can release the existing process fcntl lock.
Guard.close is cross-thread safe and idempotent; closing an older Guard again cannot clear a successor admission token.
The raw lock descriptor is closed before locking its owned PFD duplicate; constructor failures close known owners while preserving primary errors.
All publication call sites pass their actual live Guard; two target-hash/absence checks and the atomic rename occur under that cooperative protocol.
Short writes are completed and zero progress fails; a conflicting second CAS preserves the observed conflicting target.
An O_EXCL collision is never removed as if it were this operation’s temporary file.
Post-rename directory sync, read and close errors report save_outcome_unknown.
A Transaction with an uncertain result rejects another commit on the same object, and reopening reads the committed bytes.
A fresh JVM reopens the same directory left by the prior fenced published-close case and establishes a new lock.
Ordinary data/directory close uncertainty is distinguished from lock-descriptor uncertainty; the former is not falsely reported leak-free.
The README now states cooperative-writer limits and explicitly narrows the persistent process fence to uncertain lock-descriptor cleanup.
